project: Automatos AI Platform — PRD-226 The Manager's Doctrine (Auto-as-Manager wave, chain 3/6)
description: STACKED branch: ralph/prd-226-manager-doctrine ← ralph/prd-224-ticket-lane (chain 3/6; 227's wiring + 224's ASSIGN lane and ticket watches are IN your tree — the three-lane rubric you write must match how 224 actually behaves; diff scope = merge-base vs the 224 branch). Spec seeded at docs/PRDS/PRD-226-AUTO-MANAGER-DOCTRINE.md; wave map docs/PRDS/PRD-WAVE-AUTO-MANAGER.md. SCOPE = the management doctrine as content: (US-001) the 9-point doctrine into Auto's seeded soul + platform-management skill, with an idempotent hash-guarded backfill for existing workspace Auto rows; (US-002) the AutoBrain assessment prompt carries the three-lane rubric + reuse-before-create; (US-003) MissionPlanner emits 4-part dispatch contracts (OBJECTIVE·OUTPUT·TOOLS·BOUNDARIES + definition_of_done) and verification consumes the DoD when present; the ASSIGN lane's ticket-description directive shares the SAME contract fragment (single source). BAKED DECISIONS (Gerard 2026-08-27, from PRD-226 §8 proposals): Auto KEEPS the CTO voice — the doctrine is added as management sections, not a persona rewrite; narration doctrine is always-on (no per-workspace dial this wave); backfill replaces a workspace's soul ONLY when its current text hash-matches a previously shipped seed version — customized souls are SKIPPED and reported in the backfill output. THE DOCTRINE (write it from PRD-226 §4, adapted): 1 Awareness (ground answers in platform_board_summary/platform_list_missions/platform_list_agents until PRD-228's fleet tool lands) · 2 Three lanes chosen deliberately (DELEGATE=answer this conversation; ASSIGN=named single agent off-thread on the board, supervised; MISSION=multi-agent project) — say which lane and why in one line · 3 Delegate-don't-implement · 4 Reuse before creating (check the roster; honor named routing; 'one capable owner beats a duplicate'; say that you checked) · 5 Dispatch as a 4-part contract, references not pasted content · 6 Board as ledger (multi-step asks get a board card) · 7 Asks are decisions not reports (one bold sentence, options as bullets, ≤~700 chars, markdown; never idle-wait — park and move on) · 8 Recurring work becomes a playbook (propose platform_create_playbook + schedule on repetition) · 9 Narrate (one-line explanations of assignments/escalations/sign-offs). ANCHORS (verified 2026-08-27 — RE-VERIFY by grep): seeds orchestrator/core/seeds/auto-cto-custom-soul.txt + platform-management-skill.md, applied by orchestrator/core/seeds/seed_auto_agent.py:29-84 (per-workspace rows, slug auto-{workspace_id}; find its existing update/sync mechanism and follow it for the backfill); AutoBrain assessment prompt builder in orchestrator/consumers/chatbot/auto.py (rubric from 224's US-004 is already in the tree — EXTEND it, don't duplicate); planner prompt orchestrator/modules/coordination/planner.py:341,488, prompt ~:756, parse ~:1099; verification orchestrator/modules/coordination/verification.py. BINDING RULES: personas live in the DB, seed files are the source (house rule: no file hacks for DB data — the backfill writes rows); prompt fragments shared between the ASSIGN directive and the planner live in ONE place, never copy-pasted (grep must show a single definition); doctrine text changes are eval-gated — extend the LOCAL gold sets (fixtures NEVER committed: repo is public; write the eval harness additions so they load fixtures from the gitignored local path and SKIP cleanly when absent); token budget: the CHATBOT-context doctrine block stays ≤ ~350 tokens (assert a character ceiling in a test); ZERO new alembic revisions UNLESS seed_auto_agent's existing update mechanism requires a data migration — if it does, that is a hard STOP: reply RALPH_BLOCKED and say so (do not invent a migration path); NO new tables/routes; no os.getenv outside orchestrator/config.py; canonical terms; PURE tests; NEVER 'git add -A'/'git add .'/'-u'; never 'git stash -u'. No frontend stories.

userStories.title: HIGH — persona doctrine backfill is unreachable for existing workspaces (production no-op)
userStories.description: US-001's headline deliverable — the hash-guarded backfill that brings EXISTING workspace Auto rows up to the doctrine — never runs in production. `_backfill_auto_persona` is invoked only from `seed_auto_agent`'s else-branch (orchestrator/core/seeds/seed_auto_agent.py:326-329), which executes only when `seed_auto_agent` is called on an ALREADY-EXISTING Auto row. But every production caller guards on existence and calls `seed_auto_agent` ONLY when the row is ABSENT: api/chat.py:150-156 (`if row: return int(row)` precedes the call), api/workspaces.py:350-353 (`_get_or_seed_auto_agent`: `if agent: return agent` precedes the call; callers at :378/:568/:655 route through this guard), core/auth/hybrid.py:319-370 (personal-workspace CREATE path with a fresh uuid4 ws_id). So the else-branch is dead for existing rows. `sync_auto_personas` (seed_auto_agent.py:142-165) has NO production caller — grep shows only tests/test_prd226_doctrine.py:153. Existing workspaces already carry `_ALEMBIC_BACKFILL_PERSONA` rows (inserted by orchestrator/alembic/versions/seed_auto_agents_existing_workspaces.py:65-72), whose hash IS in `_KNOWN_SEED_PERSONA_HASHES` — they WOULD be updated if the backfill were reached, but nothing reaches them. Net: only brand-new workspaces get the persona-level doctrine (via the CREATE path's `_default_persona()`); every pre-existing workspace keeps its pre-226 persona. The backfill LOGIC is correct and pure-tested; only the wiring is missing. The green suite masks the gap — every backfill test calls `_backfill_auto_persona`/`sync_auto_personas`/the CREATE path DIRECTLY, none through a real caller on an existing row, so no test asserts reachability. Review pass-note (b) ('backfill runs on deploy via the seed path — customized-soul skips appear in boot logs') is false as built. Partial mitigation: the platform-management skill §17 doctrine DOES refresh to existing installs via skill_loader._maybe_refresh_builtin_skill, so Auto is not doctrine-blind — but the always-on persona block never lands. ADVISORY (code-reviewer, unverifiable from code): a transient CTO-soul persona was force-written to every auto-% row by a raw-SQL main.py startup migration 2026-04-12→04-14 (removed in commit 8c4a1f653 'stop overwriting Auto persona'); that snapshot's hash is NOT in `_KNOWN_SEED_PERSONA_HASHES`, so any surviving row carrying it would be misclassified 'customized' and skipped even once the backfill is wired.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — sync_auto_personas is now invoked from a boot/ops path: main.py `_boot_phase_1_core` (the leader-gated, once-per-deploy seed batch, reached via run_stage(DATABASE_INIT)) calls it inside `with get_db_session() as db:` which commits on exit. Grep shows the NON-test caller: main.py:267,269. This runs against EXISTING auto-% rows (sync queries them all), closing the gap where every lazy-seed caller reached seed_auto_agent only when the row was ABSENT. test_boot_phase_invokes_sync_auto_personas pins the wiring (source-reads _boot_phase_1_core; fails if the call is removed).

DONE — test_backfill_reaches_pre_existing_alembic_row_via_real_caller drives the REAL caller sync_auto_personas (the fn the boot path calls), NOT _backfill_auto_persona directly: a pre-existing row carrying _ALEMBIC_BACKFILL_PERSONA → custom_persona_prompt becomes _default_persona(); a customized row is left byte-identical; a second pass through the same caller yields {updated:0,skipped:1,current:1} with no re-mutation (idempotent).

DONE — the 2026-04-13→14 Irish-CTO soul force-written to every auto-% row by main.py's raw-SQL startup migration (UPDATE ... custom_persona_prompt = _load_cto_soul(); removed in commit 8c4a1f653) is added to _KNOWN_SEED_PERSONA_HASHES as _CTO_SOUL_APR2026_SNAPSHOT_HASH (sha256 2a5be2b5…, recovered from git 8c4a1f653~1 — the soul file was byte-stable across the whole overwrite window, so exactly one hash). PINNED not embedded (the 4288-char snapshot carries — → unicode that hand-transcription would corrupt); a provenance+repro-command comment documents it. A surviving row is now reconciled, not misclassified 'customized'. test_cto_soul_apr2026_snapshot_hash_is_a_known_seed asserts membership; end-to-end update of a hash-matching row is proven by test_backfill_updates_alembic_backfilled_default.

userStories.title: HIGH — 4-part dispatch contract hand-duplicated in platform-management-skill.md, outside the single-source guarantee
userStories.description: The skill seed restates the 4-part contract as a near-verbatim hand-copy of the shared fragment, defeating US-003's single-source rule where the tests cannot see it. platform-management-skill.md:1090-1095 (§17 point 5 'Dispatch as a contract') repeats the same four bold labels (OBJECTIVE/OUTPUT/TOOLS/BOUNDARIES), the same clause order, and the same closer ('Reference artifacts by name or id; never paste their content...') as `DISPATCH_CONTRACT_FRAGMENT` in orchestrator/modules/coordination/dispatch_contract.py:15-21 — but as an independently-maintained Markdown string, not a reference. The single-source guards are code-only: test_fragment_has_exactly_one_definition_site (tests/test_prd226_contract.py:32-47) walks .py files, and the acceptance grep (scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd226.sh:74-80) is scoped to orchestrator --include=*.py — so this Markdown duplicate is structurally invisible to the guarantee they claim to enforce. The platform-management skill is always-on (injected into every Auto chat turn) and refreshes to existing installs via skill_loader._maybe_refresh_builtin_skill. FAILURE: a future PRD edits `DISPATCH_CONTRACT_FRAGMENT` (e.g. tweaks the TOOLS bullet); the planner prompt and the ASSIGN directive pick it up automatically, but the skill keeps the old wording — Auto's own context then carries two divergent definitions of 'the dispatch contract' simultaneously, and nothing in CI catches the divergence.
acceptanceCriteria: The skill's contract description is no longer an independently-maintained copy: either §17 point 5's body is assembled from `DISPATCH_CONTRACT_FRAGMENT` at seed time (single source), OR a test asserts the four labels + the 'never paste' closer in platform-management-skill.md stay in lock-step with `DISPATCH_CONTRACT_FRAGMENT` and fails on divergence.
The single-source check (test and/or acceptance-prd226.sh) covers the Markdown seed home, not just .py files — a hand-edit that drifts the skill's contract text from the fragment fails CI.

userStories.title: MEDIUM — doctrine triplicated; the soul-file edit lands on the CTO agent, not Auto; point 7 already drifted
userStories.description: The 9-point doctrine now lives in three hand-maintained homes, and US-001's soul-file edit does not reach the agent it was written for. Homes: (1) core/seeds/auto-cto-custom-soul.txt:101-113, (2) platform-management-skill.md §17, (3) `MANAGER_DOCTRINE_BLOCK` at seed_auto_agent.py:66-76. But auto-cto-custom-soul.txt is read ONLY by seed_cto_agent.py:22-29 (the GLOBAL, admin-only CTO agent, workspace_id=None) — NOT by the per-workspace Auto agent: seed_auto_agent.py's `_load_default_persona`/`_SOUL_DOC_PATH` (:168-175, :30) are DEAD (no caller); Auto's persona is `_default_persona()` = `_FRIENDLY_FALLBACK` + `MANAGER_DOCTRINE_BLOCK` (:79-86, seeded at :313). So the soul-file doctrine feeds the CTO agent, and PRD-226 §2/§5's grounding ('Auto's persona is seeded per workspace from auto-cto-custom-soul.txt') is factually wrong. The copies have ALREADY drifted: point 7's ask-length is stated three ways — 'keep it under a screen' (soul:109), '≤ ~700 characters' (skill §17), 'short' (block). Only the nine title-anchors are pinned across homes (tests/test_prd226_doctrine.py:21-31 DOCTRINE_ANCHORS); the substantive prose is free to diverge unnoticed.
acceptanceCriteria: The dead `_load_default_persona` + `_SOUL_DOC_PATH` are removed from seed_auto_agent.py (Auto never reads the CTO soul file), OR a comment states explicitly that auto-cto-custom-soul.txt feeds the CTO agent (seed_cto_agent.py) and NOT the per-workspace Auto agent.
PRD-226 §2 and §5 are corrected to state the per-workspace Auto persona seeds from `_default_persona()` (friendly base + `MANAGER_DOCTRINE_BLOCK`), not from auto-cto-custom-soul.txt.

Point 7's ask-length guidance reads consistently across the two Auto-facing homes (skill §17 and `MANAGER_DOCTRINE_BLOCK`), or a test pins the substantive doctrine (ask-length, tool names, lane definitions) — not just the nine titles — across those homes.
